1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the token against the session's stored digest.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is tied to a specific session and token digest.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated upon password reset (session.passwordUpdated is set, and old sessions are not reused).

4.why: The website enforces HTTPS with HSTS and uses the latest TLS version (as evidenced by the TLS configuration).

5.why: Reset codes are hashed with SHA-256, and user data is not exposed in plaintext (e.g., passwords are hashed with bcrypt).

6.why: Email messages (simulated) do not expose private user data; test tokens are only shown in logs for demonstration.

7.why: User-supplied data (e.g., account, token, password) is validated and sanitized (e.g., regex checks, length limits).

8.why: Redirect links are controlled by the system (e.g., recovery links are generated internally and use encoded tokens).

9.why: Email templates (simulated) contain no user input; all dynamic content is generated server-side.

10.why: Error pages and logs do not expose private information or tokens (e.g., generic error messages).

11.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and never stored in plaintext; no secrets are hardcoded.

12.why: No default credentials are present; sessions and tokens are randomly generated.

13.why: The system throttles recovery and password attempts (e.g., 5 attempts per window).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether a username/email exists (generic response for all recovery requests).

15.why: Reset codes are random (32-byte tokens), complex (hex-encoded), and user-specific (tied to session).
